articles.title: The State of Cybersecurity in 2026: Key Segments, Insights, and Innovations
articles.summary: Featuring:   Cybersecurity is being reshaped by the expansion of cloud infrastructure, AI, distributed systems, and increasingly complex digital environments. As organizations manage more identities, devices, data, and internet-facing infrastructure, security is shifting toward continuous visibility, control, and the ability to respond to risk at scale.   This report examines how core areas of cybersecurity are evolving in response to that shift. Across identity security, telemetry management, human security, endpoint management, human risk intelligence, exposure management, email and domain security, connected device security, AI-native security operations, and cloud security, it explores how organizations are adapting to threats that increasingly move across systems, identities, and infrastructure rather than targeting a single point of failure.   Read the full report here:  https://report.papryon.com/thehackernews
articles.title_fr: L'état de la cybersécurité en 2026 : Segments clés, perspectives et innovations
articles.summary_fr: La cybersécurité est redéfinie par l'expansion du cloud, de l'IA et des environnements numériques complexes, poussant les organisations vers une visibilité et un contrôle continus. Ce rapport examine comment les domaines clés de la cybersécurité, de la sécurité des identités à la sécurité cloud, évoluent face à des menaces qui traversent les systèmes. Il met en lumière l'adaptation à des risques qui ne ciblent plus un point de défaillance unique, mais se propagent à travers les infrastructures.

articles.title: GitLab Patches Critical 9.9 AI Gateway Flaw Allowing Command Execution on Self-Hosted Servers
articles.summary: A critical flaw in GitLab's AI Gateway could let a logged-in user with Duo Agent Platform access run commands on the gateway under certain conditions, GitLab  said in an advisory .   The gateway is the service that connects a GitLab instance to AI models, and only organizations that host their own gateway need to act. The flaw is fixed in gateway versions 19.2.4, 19.3.2, and 19.4.1.   The flaw is tracked as  CVE-2026-90970 . GitLab disclosed it on October 2 and rated it critical, with a CVSS score of 9.9 out of 10.   GitLab runs AI Gateways for its customers and has already fixed them. Customers on GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, and self-managed instances that use a GitLab-hosted gateway do not need to act, the company said.   Self-managed customers can instead  host their own gateway , an option GitLab offers for keeping AI request and response data inside the customer's own environment. articles.title_fr: GitLab corrige une faille critique (9.9) dans sa passerelle IA permettant l'exécution de commandes sur les serveurs auto-hébergés
articles.summary_fr: GitLab a corrigé une faille critique (CVE-2026-90970, CVSS 9.9) dans sa passerelle IA, permettant à un utilisateur connecté d'exécuter des commandes sur les serveurs auto-hébergés sous certaines conditions. Cette passerelle connecte les instances GitLab aux modèles d'IA. Seules les organisations hébergeant leur propre passerelle doivent mettre à jour immédiatement vers les versions 19.2.4, 19.3.2 ou 19.4.1, car GitLab a déjà sécurisé les passerelles qu'il héberge pour ses clients.

articles.title: Antino Backdoor Uses Outlook and OneDrive for C2 in China-Nexus Espionage Campaign
articles.summary: Government and policy organizations across Asia have become the target of a new campaign orchestrated by a China-nexus threat actor.   The activity, which has targeted government and policy organizations in Taiwan, India, the Philippines, Cambodia, Pakistan, Thailand, and Myanmar, involves the deployment of a previously undocumented backdoor codenamed Antino. Cisco Talos is tracking the cluster under the moniker UAT-11587 .   The threat actor was first detected in September 2025 in connection with a spear-phishing campaign directed against Taiwan's academic, think tank, and civil society policy community. Since then, attacks linked to the intrusion set have expanded to target 16 entities across eight Asian countries. articles.title_fr: La porte dérobée Antino utilise Outlook et OneDrive pour le C2 dans une campagne d'espionnage liée à la Chine
articles.summary_fr: Un acteur de menace lié à la Chine cible des organisations gouvernementales et politiques à travers l'Asie avec une nouvelle porte dérobée nommée Antino. Détectée en septembre 2025, cette campagne d'espionnage utilise Antino, un backdoor Windows compilé en Rust, pour la reconnaissance et l'exécution de commandes. Il se distingue par l'utilisation d'Outlook et OneDrive pour son canal de commande et contrôle (C2).
